  "content": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/ARTIFACTS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\claude-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\ARTIFACTS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"2fa84648afedc03f3b811cb0e61d77ee1a1d52421ba3b3fa3eb435c4abd6eb89\", \"bytes\": 9622, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"artifact-types\", \"title\": \"Artifact types\", \"anchor\": \"artifact-types\", \"start_line\": 15, \"end_line\": 62, \"content\": \"## Artifact types\\n\\n\\u201cRequired\\u201d means the selected work needs coverage of that type. It does not\\nmean every change must create a new file. Reuse an existing active artifact\\nwhen its accepted meaning and scope still cover the work. Create a conditional\\nartifact only when its condition applies.\\n\\nFor an existing selected work order (WO), get its current state and next\\naction with:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nBefore implementation, check whether that work order (WO) and its linked\\ndefinitions are eligible to start:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase start --json\\n```\\n\\nThe first command reports lifecycle context without evaluating checkpoint\\ngates. The second evaluates start readiness, including the states and coverage\\nof the selected definitions. Neither command approves or starts work.\\nHere, `REPO` is the absolute repository path and `WO-ID` is the actual ID of\\nthe selected work order (WO). Use the repository's selected released evaluator.\\n\\n| Type                  | ID prefix | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                      | When needed                                                                                                                                              |\\n|-----------------------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `intent`              | `INT-`    | States the problem, intended outcome, and limits of responsibility.                                                                                                          | The work needs an accepted purpose. Reuse an intent (INT) when that purpose still applies.                                                               |\\n| `capability`          | `CAP-`    | Describes an ability that a human or agent should have.                                                                                                                      | Requirements (REQ) need a link to the capability (CAP) they support.                                                                                     |\\n| `requirement`         | `REQ-`    | States required behavior or a constraint, with a condition for acceptance.                                                                                                   | The change creates or changes an obligation. Reuse a requirement (REQ) only if its meaning stays unchanged.                                              |\\n| `specification`       | `SPEC-`   | Defines the detailed behavior, interfaces, constraints, and rejection conditions.                                                                                            | Each requirement (REQ) selected for implementation needs specification (SPEC) coverage.                                                                  |\\n| `architecture`        | `ARCH-`   | Defines system structure and boundaries needed to meet significant requirements (REQ).                                                                                       | An active architecture (ARCH) directly addresses a requirement (REQ) selected by the work order (WO).                                                    |\\n| `adr`                 | `ADR-`    | Records an architecture decision (ADR), the alternatives, and their consequences.                                                                                            | An applicable architecture (ARCH) declares that a significant decision is required.                                                                      |\\n| `verification`        | `VER-`    | Defines how requirements (REQ) will be checked and what counts as a pass.                                                                                                    | Each selected requirement (REQ) needs verification coverage. This is the verification contract (VER), not a test result.                                 |\\n| `work_order`          | `WO-`     | Defines the bounded work to execute and its governing artifacts. Approval grants work authority.                                                                             | Before execution. One work order (WO) may cover several requirements (REQ). Completed scope does not authorize later work.                               |\\n| `verification_record` | `VREC-`   | Binds work orders (WO), verification contracts (VER), evidence, and one exact candidate commit for assessment.                                                               | When verification tied to a commit is required. One record may cover several work orders (WO) at the same commit.                                        |\\n| `release_contract`    | `REL-`    | Defines permitted release scope, gates, rollback conditions, and authority limits.                                                                                           | When a release record (RLS) is proposed.                                                                                                                 |\\n| `release_record`      | `RLS-`    | Records preparation and the later release decision for verified work at one exact commit.                                                                                    | When a formal release is proposed. Preparing the record does not release the work.                                                                       |\\n| `decision`            | `DEC-`    | Records a question, options, recommendation, decision maker, affected artifacts, and the eventual answer. It can also record a deviation from one specification (SPEC) rule. | A question blocks a transition, affects more than one artifact, or must remain recorded after approval; or work cannot meet a specification (SPEC) rule. |\\n| `risk`                | `RISK-`   | Records a threat, an owner, and a next action. Scoring and categories are optional.                                                                                          | A concern needs follow-up. A separate decision (DEC) is used when the concern must block work.                                                           |\\n| `operating_contract`  | `OPS-`    | Defines continuing service, support, monitoring, or operational assurance obligations.                                                                                       | Ongoing operational commitments apply. Omitting the record does not prove those commitments have been met.                                               |\\n\\nCode, tests, acceptance scenarios, evidence files, commits, dashboards, tickets,\\nand conversations are not additional formal artifact types. They may support\\nor be referenced by formal artifacts but do not grant authority by themselves.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"47268c9ec1e3551fb547ad3d1ef7b8da0b773b52b3a4364f42c36cc64f98bf83\"}, {\"heading\": \"artifact-locations\", \"title\": \"Artifact locations\", \"anchor\": \"artifact-locations\", \"start_line\": 63, \"end_line\": 96, \"content\": \"## Artifact locations\\n\\nNew formal artifacts use these directories below\\n`docs/engineering/DOMAIN/`. `DOMAIN` is the selected domain name. These paths\\ndescribe storage, not authority; the artifact ID, metadata, and typed links\\nremain authoritative. Use the supported authoring command to obtain the actual\\npath. Do not move existing records merely to match this table.\\n\\n| Artifact | TYPE | Directory |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Intent (INT) | `intent` | `intent/` |\\n| Capability (CAP) | `capability` | `capabilities/` |\\n| Requirement (REQ) | `requirement` | `requirements/` |\\n| Specification (SPEC) | `specification` | `specifications/` |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) | `architecture` | `architecture/` |\\n| Architecture decision (ADR) | `adr` | `architecture/adr/` |\\n| Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | `verification/` |\\n| Work order (WO) | `work_order` | `work-orders/` |\\n| Verification record (VREC) | `verification_record` | `verification-records/` |\\n| Release contract (REL) | `release_contract` | `release/` |\\n| Release record (RLS) | `release_record` | `releases/` |\\n| Operating contract (OPS) | `operating_contract` | `operations/` |\\n| Decision (DEC) | `decision` | `decisions/` |\\n| Risk (RISK) | `risk` | `risks/` |\\n\\nThe same domain has `evidence/` for retained work-order evidence and\\n`acceptance/` for acceptance scenarios. These are supporting files, not new\\nformal artifact types. Legacy flat artifact locations remain readable and\\nMUST NOT be moved by an upgrade without separate authority.\\n\\nTemplates under `docs/engineering/templates/` are authoring assets. They are\\nexcluded from active-artifact validation and grant no authority. Use\\n`capture-verification` and `prepare-release` for commit-bound VREC and RLS\\ninstances; an edited template is not a substitute for their derived evidence.\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8df276d2f837c4dcc663dbdb42c67cbb6f8fe3bf4abcb53acf86bc7538269a72\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DEFINITION_LINKS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\claude-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DEFINITION_LINKS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"75b0c06f90fbb219fc31684a1a2d97987215dbada20e335656e45a57532c3010\", \"bytes\": 3505, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-between-definitions\", \"title\": \"Links between definitions\", \"anchor\": \"links-between-definitions\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 35, \"content\": \"## Links between definitions\\n\\nAn arrow points from the artifact that records the link to the artifact it\\nreferences. These links describe meaning and coverage, not execution order.\\n\\nRepository validation, draft validation and work-order preflight share the\\ndeclared source/relation/target types. A supplied undeclared relation or a target\\nof the wrong type is invalid even when no work order selects the artifact.\\nPreflight still evaluates readiness only for its selected governing chain.\\nThe read-only draft query permits specific unfinished authoring slots; ordinary\\nvalidation and approval retain their completeness requirements.\\n\\n```mermaid\\nflowchart LR\\n    CAP[\\\"Capability (CAP)\\\"] -->|derives_from| INT[\\\"Intent (INT)\\\"]\\n    REQ[\\\"Requirement (REQ)\\\"] -->|derives_from| CAP\\n    SPEC[\\\"Specification (SPEC)\\\"] -->|specifies| REQ\\n    VER[\\\"Verification contract (VER)\\\"] -->|verifies| REQ\\n    ARCH[\\\"Architecture (ARCH)\\\"] -->|addresses| REQ\\n    ARCH -->|conforms_to| SPEC\\n    ADR[\\\"Architecture decision (ADR)\\\"] -->|decides| ARCH\\n```\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Capability (CAP) \\u2192 Intent (INT) | `derives_from` | Each active capability (CAP) names one or more active intents (INT). |\\n| Requirement (REQ) \\u2192 Capability (CAP) | `derives_from` | Each active requirement (REQ) names one or more active capabilities (CAP). |\\n| Specification (SPEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `specifies` | Each requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO) needs one or more selected active specifications (SPEC). |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `addresses` | The architecture (ARCH) names every requirement (REQ) that materially drives its structure. |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `conforms_to` | For each addressed requirement (REQ), the selected architecture (ARCH) names at least one selected specification (SPEC) covering it. |\\n| Architecture decision (ADR) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) | `decides` | Each selected architecture (ARCH) that requires a design decision has at least one selected active architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Verification contract (VER) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `verifies` | Each selected requirement (REQ) has one or more selected active verification contracts (VER). |\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7e7361437700c3a1bf7d9add02accf3a4d3ee3fa48dbdc0ba0b991b40514071a\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\claude-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"design-simplicity\", \"title\": \"Design simplicity\", \"anchor\": \"design-simplicity\", \"start_line\": 21, \"end_line\": 58, \"content\": \"## Design simplicity\\n\\nFor unfinished work, `harnessctl validate-draft REPO --artifact ID --json`\\nreports whether one supported draft has an admissible shape. Only exact values\\nat the same type and field in this evaluator's canonical template, and missing\\nor empty required authoring links, can be reported as incomplete. Invalid\\nidentity, dates, metadata shapes, actual endpoints, lifecycle history and\\ndisposition are errors. A missing non-template ID is an error. Background\\nfindings remain visible; this result makes no whole-repository validity claim.\\nComplete the authoring checklist and pass ordinary approval gates before\\nrequesting approval. Draft admission grants no authority to write or approve.\\n\\nChoose the least complex design that satisfies the agreed requirements and\\nconstraints. Justify material added complexity by the need it serves and why\\na simpler approach is insufficient. Consider the effort to understand, build,\\ntest, operate and change the whole solution. Defer speculative needs. Review\\nboth the necessity of the specified behavior and the simplicity of its\\nimplementation. Preserve correctness and the project's required quality and\\nsafety properties.\\n\\nStart from the smallest complete solution. Each project supplies its agreed\\nusers, scale, operating conditions and quality constraints. Agreed future needs\\ncan matter; imagined flexibility alone is insufficient. Credible risk analysis\\ncan justify prevention before an incident. Fewer lines, shorter specifications\\nor fewer tests do not establish simplicity; moving work to users, operations\\nor dependencies also has a cost.\\n\\nApply the relevant questions below before definition approval and during design\\nand implementation review. Return unjustified obligations or design complexity\\nfor revision through the existing decision process. Explain material choices\\nin the existing specification, design or review: the need, why a simpler option\\nis insufficient and the added cost. Scale the explanation to the decision; a\\nsmall choice may need one sentence, a significant design may use its existing\\narchitecture decision. Trivial changes need no separate comparison document.\\n\\nThese are human review standards. They introduce no separate KISS artifact,\\nmandatory score, receipt, automated simplicity gate or additional approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"29e9b6296f39215c4b2ad36659c0674f0b20650682db9aa1187fc97871cfdb06\"}, {\"heading\": \"intent\", \"title\": \"intent\", \"anchor\": \"intent\", \"start_line\": 76, \"end_line\": 84, \"content\": \"## intent\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain the present problem, who it affects, and the outcome wanted.\\n- What is the smallest useful outcome, and which needs and constraints are actually agreed?\\n- Say how the owner will know the change helped; an honest baseline may be `not measured`.\\n- State the important scope limits. Create a new intent when the desired outcome changes.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"291e8274f0c400a3d2d1ecdd56f2c10d68ab6cb40f667076a034e44d87c05e42\"}, {\"heading\": \"capability\", \"title\": \"capability\", \"anchor\": \"capability\", \"start_line\": 85, \"end_line\": 93, \"content\": \"## capability\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Say what an actor should be able to do and any relevant conditions.\\n- Does each supported case serve an agreed need under those conditions?\\n- Link the intent it serves. The graph lists the derived requirements.\\n- Put implementation details where they help the implementer; no required `can ... under` wording.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ee6452eeeb618cbe10c941638e7f6be38d2709f53e169920c2d3d012c94ce978\"}, {\"heading\": \"requirement\", \"title\": \"requirement\", \"anchor\": \"requirement\", \"start_line\": 59, \"end_line\": 75, \"content\": \"## requirement\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- State the observable behavior and why it is needed. Ordinary language is accepted; `SHALL` is optional.\\n- What agreed outcome does this obligation serve, for whom and under which conditions? Separate requirements from assumptions and speculative needs.\\n- Include a concrete acceptance condition in `Examples`, `Acceptance`, `measure`, `verification_notes`, or a linked verification contract.\\n- Name the source capability and a verification method. Supported method arrays contain `test`, `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration`; retained text methods remain readable.\\n- Replace unfinished placeholders and resolve blocking decisions before approval.\\n\\n### Guidance\\n\\nWrite enough for someone to implement and check the behavior. Use the template's\\nsections when helpful. Word counts, sentence shapes and numbers of code references\\nare not checked. Writing hints never block approval. Optional metadata must still\\nhave a valid value when supplied.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"333872b200842af881c6c22cfcb0631897071421f423885b2702ac6b72c75770\"}, {\"heading\": \"specification\", \"title\": \"specification\", \"anchor\": \"specification\", \"start_line\": 94, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"## specification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain what an implementation must do, including meaningful failure behavior.\\n- Is each promised behavior necessary? Could a simpler contract meet the agreed need? Prescribe a mechanism only when it is a necessary constraint.\\n- Link the requirements and show an example someone can check.\\n- Give a rule a stable identifier when evidence or a decision needs to refer to it.\\n- Check that supplied rule references exist and identifiers are unambiguous.\\n\\nMissing summaries and ambiguous rule references may produce draft hints. Hints\\nhelp a reviewer; they do not withhold approval. Existing approved text need not\\nbe rewritten to adopt these checklists.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7aeefa5f4ed363ecdef5185d2b776c6fdd9146ece8e2bfd7ae1ee852f0acf6e1\"}, {\"heading\": \"verification\", \"title\": \"verification\", \"anchor\": \"verification\", \"start_line\": 126, \"end_line\": 135, \"content\": \"## verification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Independence: expected values derive from the requirements and specifications, never from candidate output.\\n- A requirement-to-evidence matrix with a pass condition per requirement.\\n- Cover normal behavior and meaningful failure outcomes or risks; do not invent failure scenarios to fill a template.\\n- What accepted behavior or quality does each test or CI check establish? Cover distinct relevant outcomes, reuse applicable evidence, and avoid mirroring every implementation branch or combination.\\n- Pass criteria name the platforms and the evaluator.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e6d36e5fe7a23845861e67079317f856b4f892d7f17c4f3d4dbdb4476edb7720\"}, {\"heading\": \"work_order\", \"title\": \"work_order\", \"anchor\": \"work_order\", \"start_line\": 136, \"end_line\": 146, \"content\": \"## work_order\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `[execution_scope].paths` is exact: files or component-prefix directories, nothing wider.\\n- `[assurance]` is classified and its rationale names what later decisions depend on.\\n- In scope and out of scope are both stated; the decision envelope says what the implementer may and may not decide.\\n- Stop conditions and the completion report format are stated.\\n- Is every planned change needed for the agreed outcome? Include removal or adjustment of obsolete behavior, tests and instructions within the approved scope.\\n- Inspect supporting paths before approval and assess the supplied plan through [Draft work orders](harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Keep reasons in Expected change surface; do not add a separate planning artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8d3be9bfae6d0679a08544ac587fa73e1a26e026d23373c29e1927e0803e7b8\"}, {\"heading\": \"release_contract\", \"title\": \"release_contract\", \"anchor\": \"release_contract\", \"start_line\": 157, \"end_line\": 163, \"content\": \"## release_contract\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `gates` names every work order the release may include.\\n- Version, rollback conditions, and evidence expectations are explicit.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c9c8d32b5f3c5b73f05f5d2cd120379bb50e81625a8d58d6c4d1ce25529a61f5\"}]}]}",
  "is_error": false

  "content": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\claude-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"c4ffde0efff3a57df41cf6b282896e6827ea289607f8b73faa8f7c09d0c70213\", \"bytes\": 8654, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nDefinitions, work scope and verification requirements are ready for work planning.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3977586afdaba8e900cfd38bfd72b02ccf3d011048dae4b247fe81a24c64c9cc\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nRead [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#links-from-work-orders-wo](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#links-from-work-orders-wo), [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope) and [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity) and [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#work_order](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#work_order).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d2a9a7707114a465ebde20884e2a996807663ab4aa94ff11008f2360617efe50\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements\", \"title\": \"Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 143, \"content\": \"### Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements\\n\\n**Inputs:** The outcome, scope, artifact inventory, definition drafts,\\namendment proposals, verification contracts (VER), risks (RISK), and\\nunresolved decisions (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New or completed work orders (WO) in `draft`.\\n  Applicable risks (RISK) and open decisions (DEC) updated with the actual\\n  work order (WO) links. Lifecycle states and dispositions are preserved.\\n  Approved work orders (WO) remain unchanged; proposed scope changes require\\n  review.\\n- **Transient working material:** The review handoff and evaluator results.\\n  Retain these under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Inspect the implementation and follow its callers, references and consumers.\\n   Check tests and fixtures, instructions and documentation, packaging and CI,\\n   and verification outputs where they apply. Keep the working inventory in\\n   the conversation or temporary storage outside the repository.\\n   Group each complete, independently verifiable outcome into one bounded\\n   work order with its necessary supporting changes.\\n2. Select an existing work order (WO) in `draft` for a unit only if its scope\\n   matches. Otherwise, create a new work order (WO) with the commands below.\\n3. Complete each draft using the field table below. In Expected change\\n   surface, name the inspected paths and give a short reason for each.\\n   Explain non-applicable areas and unknown destinations briefly.\\n4. Check that every selected requirement (REQ) has the specification (SPEC)\\n   and verification contract (VER) coverage defined in [Complete work scope](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope).\\n5. Apply `## work_order` \\u2192 `### Checklist` in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n6. Add the new work order (WO) IDs to applicable `threatens` relations in risks\\n   (RISK) and `concerns` or `blocks` relations in open decisions (DEC). Keep\\n   every blocked ID in `concerns`. Preserve any required pairing between the\\n   risk (RISK) and decision (DEC).\\n7. If the planned change needs a missing release or operating contract,\\n   use [Prepare a release or operating contract](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract) now that the work\\n   order IDs exist. Include its draft in the proposed package.\\n8. Run the validation command below.\\n9. Correct findings within the proposed drafts. Rerun validation after edits.\\n   Report unrelated findings separately. Retain findings that need a decision\\n   or an accepted-definition amendment as unresolved dependencies.\\n10. Run the selected-work check below for each proposed work order (WO).\\n    Supply every planned file from Expected change surface with\\n    `--planned-path`. Inspect `scope.preparation`: resolve uncovered or\\n    invalid paths in the draft before requesting approval. A successful\\n    command exit does not establish coverage or a complete impact analysis.\\n    Explain future generated destinations using\\n    [Generated outputs](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#generated-outputs).\\n11. Present the outcome, scope, artifact IDs and paths, validation results,\\n    unresolved decisions (DEC), and unapplied amendments. Include the\\n    evaluator's reported next action for each selected work order (WO).\\n\\n| Field or section | Content |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `Objective` | The outcome this work order (WO) will deliver. |\\n| `In scope` / `Out of scope` | The boundaries from [Define the limits of the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#define-the-limits-of-the-change) assigned to this work order (WO). |\\n| `Constraints` | The conditions from [Define the limits of the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#define-the-limits-of-the-change) that apply to this work. |\\n| `Expected change surface` | Inspected planned paths, the reason for each, and unresolved destinations. |\\n| `[execution_scope].paths` | Exact repository-relative files or component directories ending in `/`.
