The JSON report always carries `advisories` and `advisory_count`. On a repository whose definitions are all approved, `Advisories: 0` is the normal reading. Since 0.18.0 the approval transition of a draft intent, capability, requirement or specification is refused while any advisory remains on it (`QGP-G1-AUTHORING`, `QGP-G2-AUTHORING`, `SPEC-TCM-007`); the refusal names each advisory and ends with `fix the draft and run the transition again`. `validate` itself keeps passing.\n150\t\n151\tInspection reuses the existing validator and Harness Explorer snapshot. It\n152\treports `mode = repository_wide`, no selected artifact, formal validity, ready\n153\tdecisions, draft definitions, active work, assurance preparation, and existing\n154\trepository findings. Human output groups repeated rule instances for\n155\treadability; `--json` retains every finding. Inspection output MUST NOT be used\n156\tas selected-iteration restitution.\n157\t\n158\tThe `assurance_pending` queue contains only an `implemented` work order whose explicit `[assurance]` classification is `required` and which has no direct `ready`, `verified`, or `released` VREC coverage. It suggests non-automatic preparation after one clean candidate commit; it does not select aggregate scope, create a record, or make the assurance decision. Completed legacy work without a classification and work explicitly classified `not_required` are not inferred into this queue.\n159\t\n160\tThe temporal reassessment observation `W-HEX-003` is deliberately narrow: it compares dates only for supported declared dependency relations whose source can still be meaningfully reassessed. It does not reopen completed work orders, reinterpret commit-bound verification or release records, or treat derived graph projections as declared dependencies.\n161\t\n162\tFor existing lifecycle queues and a closed set of actionable derived warning rules, inspection also reports deterministic suggested next steps. Each suggestion identifies its source, affected artifacts, action class, accountable role, and `automatic = false`. Suggestions contain no executable command and never assert eligibility or authority. Validator findings, informational observations, and unknown rules remain visible without guessed advice.\n163\t\n164\tInspection ends with a vocabulary section. It counts the words of every artifact's statement and body with code removed, drops common English and the harness terms the managed instructions define, and names the project terms at or above `--vocabulary-threshold` occurrences (default 50, between 30 and 100) that have no entry in `GLOSSARY.md` at the repository root, and the entries whose term appears in no artifact. The glossary is repository content. Published repository-copy installations seed it empty; minimal external-resource installation creates no glossary. Both routes preserve an existing glossary. The section is informational and never blocks.\n165\t\n166\tA successfully produced inspection exits zero even when formal validation failed or attention exists, so use `validate` when gate exit behavior is required. Inspection is repository-local derived evidence: it does not approve, authorize, verify, supersede, release, remediate, or independently govern the repository.\n167\t\n168\tDashboard defaults to `target/harness-dashboard/`; its generated files are derived evidence, not formal authority. The small `index.html` bootstrap verifies `dashboard-manifest.json`, then loads a summary, compact topology, readiness data, individual artifact details, and explicitly expanded evidence from digest-named static resources. Serve the directory from one HTTP origin, for example with `python -m http.server 8000 --directory target/harness-dashboard`; direct `file://` opening is intentionally rejected because progressive resource loading and integrity checks require an origin. Generation remains local and needs no application server, but publishing or sharing the directory exposes every manifest-declared artifact and evidence body; the command does not scan for secrets or redact repository material. Doctor checks the standard installed contract against `.engineering-harness.lock` and the current distribution.\n169\t\n170\t## Standalone draft validation\n171\t\n172\t```text\n173\tharnessctl validate-draft [TARGET] --artifact ARTIFACT-ID [--json]\n174\t```\n175\t\n176\tThe caller supplies a complete projection. The command uses one parsed catalog\n177\tand the executing evaluator's canonical templates. It writes nothing. JSON is\n178\t`se-harness-draft-validation-v1`, with `selection` (id, type, status, relative\n179\tpath), `admissible`, `errors`, `incomplete`, and `background`. Findings include\n180\tstable codes and structured field/relation/target details where relevant.\n181\tText reports the same facts. Exit 0 means admissible; 1 means a produced refusal;\n182\t2 means usage or a failure before a result can be produced.\n183\t\n184\tSupported draft types: intent, capability, requirement, specification,\n185\tarchitecture, adr, verification, work_order, release_contract and\n186\toperating_contract. Decision, risk, verification_record and release_record\n187\tcontinue through their existing commands.\n188\t\n189\tA requirement with `CAP-xxx`, an omitted `derives_from`, or an empty array can\n190\tbe admissible with an incomplete finding. A link to an existing release record,\n191\tan unknown non-template target, or `[\"CAP-xxx\", \"RLS-SEH-001\"]` is refused.\n192\tMalformed TOML and duplicate IDs block a trustworthy catalog globally. Other\n193\tunselected findings remain background. A correct endpoint does not establish\n194\treadiness of its full governing chain.\n195\t\n196\tSelection outside draft, lifecycle history and disposition are refused. This\n197\tsnapshot query cannot prove that imported identity or provenance is unchanged.\n198\tThe hosted caller must compare protected fields to its immutable base and enforce\n199\trights and expected versions. Admission does not waive validation, approval,\n200\tverification or release gates, and includes no lifecycle next step.\n201\t\n202\t<a id=\"released-resource-lookup-successor-candidate\"></a>\n203\t\n204\t## Released resource lookup\n205\t\n206\tReleased evaluators since 0.21.0 provide this command for repositories selecting\n207\tthe `released-resources-v1` layout. This repository uses independently installed\n208\t0.22.1 after explicit adoption under WO-HUP-030. Publication alone does not\n209\tchange a repository's selection.\n210\t\n211\t```text\n212\tharnessctl resources [TARGET] [--resource RESOURCE-ID] [--content] [--json]\n213\t```\n214\t\n215\tWithout `--resource`, list resource IDs, local paths, byte digests and headings\n216\tfrom the exact selected release. Use a returned ID with `--resource` to select\n217\tone item. `--content` requires that one ID; it does not return every guide at\n218\tonce. For `ENGINEERING_HARNESS.md`, it renders the project and selected version\n219\tin memory. No instruction copy or lifecycle state is written to the repository.\n220\t\n221\tJSON output uses `se-harness-resources-v1`, with the selected `release` identity\n222\tand `resources` array. Content requests also return `content` and\n223\t`content_sha256`. Missing, altered or mismatched selected resources cause a\n224\trefusal; the command does not install resources or borrow another release.\n225\t\n226\t## Work readiness\n227\t\n228\t```text\n229\tharnessctl preflight [TARGET] --work-order WO-... [--phase start|review] [--json]\n230\tharnessctl select-work-order --event GITHUB_EVENT_PATH [--json]\n231\t```\n232\t\n233\t`start` is the default phase. Preflight checks lifecycle eligibility, the governing chain, and the selected work order's explicit `[assurance]` declaration, then displays the classification, rationale, and deciding role with the reading manifest. A selected work order without a valid declaration fails even when completed legacy validation remains compatible. Passing proves structural readiness only; it does not prove comprehension, semantic scope fit, implementation correctness, the truth of the rationale or role claim, assurance, or release.\n234\t\n235\t`select-work-order` reads one bounded event file. A body uses either\n236\t`Harness-Work-Order: WO-AAA-001` or\n237\t`Harness-Work-Orders: WO-AAA-001, WO-BBB-002`. Use `--field work-orders`\n238\tfor one ID per output line. LF and CRLF are equivalent. Both declarations\n239\ttogether, duplicate IDs and malformed IDs are rejected.\n240\t\n241\t```sh\n242\tharnessctl check-pr [TARGET] --event EVENT.json --from-git BASE [--json]\n243\t```\n244\t\n245\t`check-pr` evaluates every selected approved work order and the complete diff\n246\tagainst their combined scope. Unrelated changes are not admitted by listing\n247\tanother work order; that work order must actually cover the path. In-progress\n248\twork also needs passing local handoff checks. CI calls this command directly.\n249\t\n250\t\n251\t## Selected-scope workflow execution\n252\t\n253\tThe command shapes below are stable interfaces. The candidate standard\n254\t[`CONTINUE.md`](../../templates/repository/standard/docs/engineering/harness/CONTINUE.md#continue-selected-work)\n255\troutes to the selected procedure, and\n256\t[`WORKFLOW.json`](../../templates/repository/standard/docs/engineering/WORKFLOW.json)\n257\tis the machine-readable contract loaded by `harnessctl`. Use the workflow rule\n258\tselected for the artifact's exact type, state, and direct related records. Do\n259\tnot derive a new transition or next action from this reference.\n260\t\n261\t```text\n262\tharnessctl evidence [TARGET] --artifact WO-... --checkpoint start|pre-action|transition|handoff \\\n263\t  [--rebound-at RFC3339] [--json]\n264\tharnessctl pr-body [TARGET] --artifact WO-... [--json]\n265\tharnessctl check [TARGET] [--artifact WO-...|VREC-...|RLS-...] [--json] [--include-background]  # without a checkpoint: the projection\n266\tharnessctl check [TARGET] --artifact WO-... --planned-path PATH [--planned-path PATH ...] [--json]\n267\tharnessctl check [TARGET] --artifact WO-...|VREC-...|RLS-... \\\n268\t  --checkpoint start|pre-action|transition|handoff|scope [--target STATE] \\  # with a checkpoint:\n269\t  [--procedure PROC-...] [--from-git BASE | --changed-path PATH ... \\\n270\t  [--changes-complete] | --change-manifest PATH] [--pull-request-body PATH] [--json]\n271\tharnessctl transition [TARGET] --set ID=STATUS --decision ID=ACTOR \\\n272\t  [--set ID=STATUS ...] [--decision ID=ACTOR ...] [--reason ID=TEXT ...] \\\n273\t  [--apply] [--json]\n274\t```\n275\t\n276\t`check` without `--checkpoint` is the one call an agent makes first (`WO-ECP-001`,\n277\tfolded from `next` by `WO-ECP-019`). It returns the projection of the selected artifact — the single\n278\t`in_progress` work order when `--artifact` is absent, otherwise `WEX-ECP-001` names the candidate\n279\tcount — with an additive `context` object: `reading_manifest` (the preflight manifest for the\n280\tphase the state implies, `start` for `approved` and `in_progress`, `review` afterwards),\n281\t`governing`, `declared_paths`, `state`, `next` (`argv`, `procedure_id`, `step_id`, the same step a\n282\tcheckpoint `check` selects) and `decision_required`. It writes nothing and needs no prior command.\n283\tThe human block renders the context as a `Context` section after `Command or response`, and\n284\t`result_sha256` binds it. The former `next` command was removed after 0.11.0 (`WO-ECP-020`); its\n285\ttombstone guard left with 0.15.0 (`WO-ECP-025`), so the parser now refuses the name as unknown.\n286\t\n287\t`check` without `--checkpoint` projects only the selected artifact's governing chain and direct\n288\tlifecycle dependencies. It uses the ordered recommendation registry in\n289\t`WORKFLOW.json`. For example, `WFL-WO-READY-VREC` takes precedence over\n290\t`WFL-WO-PREPARE-VREC`, so existing ready assurance coverage cannot produce a\n291\tduplicate-capture recommendation. Unrelated repository findings remain a\n292\tbackground count; `--include-background` expands categories without making\n293\tthem selected-scope work.\n294\t\n295\tThe optional `--planned-path` view assesses proposed files before approval.\n296\tIt requires an explicit work order and no checkpoint. Repeat the option for\n297\teach repository-relative file in the plan; the file need not exist yet.\n298\tExisting calls without this option are unchanged.\n299\t\n300\tThe schema-2 result adds `scope.preparation`: `planned_paths`, `coverage`\n301\t(`covered`, `uncovered` or `invalid`), `explicit_matches` with the matching\n302\t`scope_entry`, `automatic_matches` with the existing admission rule,\n303\t`uncovered_paths`, `invalid_declarations` and\n304\t`impact_analysis: \"not_assessed\"`. These machine fields participate in the\n305\tresult digest. The human report lists coverage and each path's reason.\n306\t\n307\tThe normal lifecycle projection, next action, exit meaning and gate fields\n308\tare preserved. **Exit zero does not mean the plan is covered.** Inspect\n309\t`scope.preparation.coverage` and resolve uncovered or invalid paths before\n310\trequesting approval. Coverage cannot prove that the agent found every\n311\taffected file. Planning writes nothing and does not populate actual changed\n312\tpaths, assert completeness, evaluate gates or authorize work.\n313\t\n314\tThe selected WO file and existing directly linked VREC/RLS records and their\n315\tdeclared evaluator evidence use their existing exact-path admission rules.\n316\tThe selected WO's own packet directory is reported separately under its\n317\texisting admission rule.\n318\tAn unallocated future record has no assessable path; explain its expected\n319\trelationship rule and check the actual destination after preparation.\n320\tOther review/log evidence needs explicit scope unless an existing rule covers\n321\tit. A neighboring file is not admitted by a generated record's directory.\n322\t\n323\tDo not combine planned paths with `--checkpoint`, `--target`, `--procedure`,\n324\t`--changed-path`, `--changes-complete`, `--change-manifest`, `--from-git`\n325\tor `--pull-request-body`. Invalid selection, malformed paths, case duplicates,\n326\tdirectory inputs and repository escapes are refused through normal diagnostics.\n327\tThis option must be used with a released evaluator that provides it; candidate\n328\tsource tests do not change the repository's selected evaluator.\n329\t\n330\tWith a checkpoint, `check` resolves the first matching rule, its typed `PROC-*` procedure, and its\n331\t`QG-*` gates; `--checkpoint scope` evaluates only the scope predicates of\n332\t`QG-G4-IMPLEMENTATION-EVIDENCE` for a work order in any lifecycle state and\n333\twrites nothing, which is what the managed pull-request gate runs (`WO-ECP-013`); [`harnessctl check` explained](harnessctl-check.md) walks\n334\tthrough the checkpoints, the rule table, the gates, and the refusal codes. `--checkpoint transition --target STATE` previews, read-only, the\n335\texact predicates and graph-structural checks `transition --set ID=STATE` will\n336\tevaluate (`WO-ECP-009`): the transition binding index of `QUALITY_GATES.json`\n337\tkeyed by artifact family and target state, evaluated by the same gate evaluator\n338\twith the same context, plus the `QGS-*` checks under the synthetic\n339\t`QG-STRUCTURAL` gate. A transition whose evaluation is not all `pass` renders\n340\t`Blocked by` with each refusing predicate's own identifier and writes nothing;\n341\tan applied transition that would be blocked fails closed with that identifier. `pre-action` requires `--procedure`, which must equal the selected\n342\tprocedure or one complete declared alternative. `--changed-path` may repeat;\n343\t`--changes-complete` asserts that the supplied set is complete, including an\n344\tempty set. The assertion is evidence, not proof from a trusted Git baseline.\n345\tWithout it, path-scope predicates are `not_assessable`.\n346\t\n347\t`--from-git BASE` derives the change set from Git instead of from typed\n348\tpaths: the union of `git diff --name-only BASE` against the working tree\n349\t(renames contribute both names) and the untracked files Git does not ignore,\n350\teach normalized as above; the set is complete by construction and the result\n351\trecords `change_set_source = \"git\"`. It is mutually exclusive with the\n352\tchanged-path options and the manifest (`WEX-ECP-002`); outside a Git\n353\tcheckout, with a base Git cannot resolve, or on any Git failure it blocks\n354\twith `WEX-ECP-003` and evaluates no predicate as `pass`. The selected work\n355\torder's own artifact file, written by its lifecycle transitions and so always\n356\tin the diff, is admitted to its scope by construction (`ECP-CHG-007`).\n357\t\n358\t`evidence` writes `DOMAIN/evidence/WO-ID/WO-ID-CHECKPOINT.md` (`WO-ECP-002`):\n359\ta fenced TOML header at byte offset 0 with exactly `artifact`, `checkpoint`,\n360\t`formal_snapshot_sha256` and `rebound_at`, followed by an owner-authored\n361\tbody. On an existing packet only the header bytes change; the body is\n362\tretained byte for byte, and a file without a header at offset 0, with a\n363\theader naming another artifact or checkpoint, or with invalid TOML is refused\n364\t(`WEX-ECP-010`). It refuses when a `.gitattributes` rule would convert the\n365\tpacket's line endings (`WEX-ECP-011`) and when the single `in_progress` work\n366\torder is not the one named (`WEX-ECP-012`). `QGP-G4I-EVIDENCE` reads that\n367\theader through a TOML parser; a packet without one is not assessable, and\n368\tthe message names the `evidence` command that writes the header (the\n369\tone-release substring grace closed under `WO-AUT-006`). `check --checkpoint handoff\n370\t--from-git BASE` is self-binding (`ECP-SBH-001` to `-006`): it rebinds an\n371\texisting packet header to the current formal snapshot before evaluating —\n372\tbody preserved, `evidence`'s `WEX-ECP-010`/`WEX-ECP-011` guards unchanged,\n373\tno packet created — and evaluates the change set with the retained result\n374\tpath included, so one run is the declared, digest-stable result. A\n375\tcompleted run retains its schema-2 result as `handoff.json` in the same\n376\tdirectory, written by the harness; that directory is admitted to the work\n377\torder's scope by construction.\n378\t\n379\t`pr-body` emits the pull-request body for an approved or later work order\n380\t(`WEX-ECP-014` otherwise): the standalone `Harness-Work-Order` line first, one\n381\tstandalone `Harness-Restitution` line carrying the retained `handoff.json`'s\n382\t`result_sha256` when it exists, then the seeded `## Summary` and\n383\t`## Verification` headings with every evidence path under the packet\n384\tdirectory. LF line endings only; the body round-trips through\n385\t`select-work-order` unchanged, so paste its output rather than typing it.\n386\t\n387\t`--change-manifest` is mutually exclusive with both changed-path options. It\n388\tmust be an in-repository UTF-8 JSON object containing only `schema` with value\n389\t`se-harness-change-set-v1`, Boolean `complete`, and ordered array `paths`.\n390\tPaths use `/`, exact-file or component-boundary directory-prefix matching, and\n391\treject absolute, traversal, backslash, wildcard, drive, URI, control-character,\n392\treserved-device, duplicate, and case-ambiguous forms.\n393\t\n394\t`check` always emits `se-harness-workflow-result-v2`. That structured result is\n395\tauthoritative. The deterministic direct human renderer uses `Outcome`, `Done`,\n396\t`Not done`, conditional `Blocked by`, `Current lifecycle state`, `Decision\n397\trequired`, `Next`, `Command or response`, and conditional `Alternatives` in\n398\tthat order. Exact-format consumers must use this renderer directly rather than\n399\task a model to transcribe it. `check`, `transition`, `capture-verification`,\n400\tand `prepare-release` emit the same `se-harness-workflow-result-v2` result\n401\tthrough one selector (`WO-ECP-005`); the former `--result-schema` option is\n402\tgone and passing it is an argument error. Each rule in `WORKFLOW.json` carries\n403\tonly the `done` and `current_lifecycle_state` prose of its restitution; the\n404\tnext step and the command come from the bound procedure.\n405\t\n406\tWhen `check` is blocked, `Next` and `Command or response` carry the corrective\n407\tform the contract declares for the first failing predicate: a command that\n408\tdiffers from the evaluated one (for example the handoff check with\n409\t`--changed-path` and `--changes-complete`), an escalation naming a decision\n410\tright, or a response describing the evidence to retain. The evaluated command\n411\tis never rendered as its own retry. Every schema-2 result carries\n412\t`result_sha256`. New results declare `digest_format = \"machine-fields-v1\"`\n413\tand hash stable machine fields rather than human wording. Retained results\n414\twithout the marker keep their original human-block digest; a pull-request body may declare it on one standalone\n415\t`Harness-Restitution:` line for CI to recompute. At `handoff`, a work order\n416\twhose `ready` verification record binds a commit no longer reachable from\n417\t`HEAD` is blocked with `W-ADS-002`; `--pull-request-body` additionally reports\n418\t`W-ADS-001` when the work-order trailer ends with a carriage return.\n419\t\n420\tAn agent-facing handoff may adapt wording, ordering, headings, and relevant\n421\texplanation or omit empty fields. It remains conforming only when it preserves\n422\tactual artifact IDs, outcome, observed effects, incomplete work, material\n423\tnon-effects, blockers, final lifecycle state, the accountable decision,\n424\tcommand argument boundaries or suggested-response meaning, and exactly one\n425\trecommended next action. Workflow-declared alternatives remain separate from\n426\tthat recommendation. Agent prose never becomes lifecycle authority.\n427\t\n428\t`transition` resolves IDs from formal metadata and plans by default. Each\n429\tselected ID needs one actor assertion. Rejection needs a non-empty reason; VREC\n430\tsupersession uses the reason as the exact successor VREC ID. A packet is\n431\tassessed as one proposed final graph. `--apply` rechecks every input byte,\n432\tproves the locked released-evaluator authority before writing, stages\n433\tsame-filesystem replacements outside artifact discovery, and rolls back earlier\n434\treplacements if a later write fails.\n435\t\n436\tThe command records actor text as an assertion, not proof of authority. The\n437\teffects and non-effects for each state are defined only by the matching\n438\t`WORKFLOW.json` rule. Related artifacts require separate explicit selection,\n439\tpassing gates, and authority.\n440\t\n441\tDirect human and JSON output are rendered from the same semantic workflow\n442\tresult. Schema 2 always identifies exactly one typed next step and derives its\n443\tcommand argument array or response from the selected procedure. Adaptive agent\n444\tpresentation consumes that result; it does not replace or recompute it.\n445\t\n446\t## Decision disposition\n447\t\n448\t```text\n449\tharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--revisit TEXT] [--apply] [--json]\n450\tharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO ... --revisit TEXT --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--apply]\n451\tharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --withdraw --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--apply]\n452\t```\n453\t\n454\tA decision artifact (`DEC-`) records one pending question, or one implementation deviation from one rule of one specification. While it is `open`, every artifact named in its `blocks` relation is refused its transitions by the `QGP-*-DECISION` predicate of the gate that transition would pass. The refusal names the decision, its question, its options, the deciding role, and the `decide` command that clears it.\n455\t\n456\t`decide` is the only way a decision changes state; `transition` refuses it. Without `--apply` the command plans and reports; with `--apply` it writes the `[disposition]` table (the option, its label, the actual human, the time, and the verbatim reason) and one lifecycle event. `--option` must name one of the options the artifact declares. A deferral needs one `--scope` entry per transition it admits and a `--revisit` trigger; the scoped transitions pass, every other blocked transition still waits. Accepting a deviation needs `--revisit`, because acceptance is time-bounded. An ineligible owner is refused with `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`.\n457\t\n458\t`--decision ACTOR` records the actual human who made the decision. With\n459\t`--authority-owner OWNER`, the evaluator checks OWNER against the existing\n460\tholders for the blocked artifacts, or the departed specification for a\n461\tdeviation. OWNER must match exactly and contain non-blank printable text of\n462\tat most 128 characters. It is retained separately as `authority_owner` in\n463\tthe disposition. Without the option, ACTOR must directly match a holder.\n464\tBoth preview and apply use the same checks. The CLI does not authenticate\n465\tthese claims or grant consent; the caller must first establish the human's\n466\tauthority and obtain the exact decision. Existing owner labels and historical\n467\trecords are not changed.\n468\t\n469\tThe validator reports a malformed decision as `E-DCM-001` to `E-DCM-003`, prose in a legacy definition's `## Open decisions` section as `E-DCM-004`, a deviation whose `against` fragment is not a rule identifier of the named specification (`SPEC-xxx#PREFIX-AREA-NNN`) as `E-DCM-005`, and an accepted deviation past its revisit or accepted twice against the same rule as `W-DCM-001` and `W-DCM-002`. See [decision artifacts](decision-artifacts.md) for the model.\n470\t\n471\tWhen the decision concerns a raised risk, `--apply` also moves that risk to the state the option names, in the same act: `accept` needs `--revisit`, `mitigate` needs `--mitigated-by WO-...`, and `avoid` records `--avoided-by` (an ADR or a decision; it defaults to the disposing decision). A deferral leaves the risk `raised`; a withdrawal withdraws it.\n472\t\n473\t## Risk recording\n474\t\n475\t```text\n476\tharnessctl raise-risk [TARGET] --domain SLUG --title TEXT --stage STAGE --category CATEGORY --cause TEXT --effect TEXT --likelihood N --impact N --threatens ID [--threatens ID ...] --raised-by ACTOR [--owner ROLE ...] [--id RISK-...] [--with-decision [--decision-id DEC-...] [--recommend accept|avoid|mitigate]] [--dry-run] [--json]\n477\tharnessctl risks [TARGET] --artifact ID [--json]\n478\t```\n479\t\n480\tA risk artifact (`RISK-`) records one measured threat: one cause, one effect, the stage it threatens, `likelihood` and `impact` from 1 to 5, and their product as `score`. `raise-risk` computes the score, writes the file in `raised` and records the raise as a lifecycle event, in one act; a measurement outside the range or an identifier already declared anywhere is refused before anything is written, exit 2. `--domain` takes the domain slug or the identifier token of exactly one domain. With `--with-decision` the command also writes the open decision that blocks the threatened artifacts, with the options `accept`, `avoid` and `mitigate`. No gate reads risks: the stop is the paired decision's `QGP-*-DECISION` predicate, and the refusal names the decision, not the risk.\n481\t\n482\t`risks` lists every risk threatening the named artifact or, for a work order, its governing chain; it writes nothing.\n483\t\n484\tThe validator reports a missing or invalid field as `E-RSK-001`, a wrong measurement or score as `E-RSK-002`, a raised risk that no pending decision names as `E-RSK-003`, a paired decision whose `blocks` differs from the risk's `threatens` as `E-RSK-004`, a disposition typed by hand as `E-RSK-005`, and an accepted risk past its revisit as `W-RSK-001`. See [risk artifacts](risk-artifacts.md) for the model.\n485\t\n486\t## Safe repository upgrade\n487\t\n488\t```text\n489\tharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] [--json]\n490\tharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] --apply [--json]\n491\tharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] --apply --work-order WO-... --evidence-output docs/engineering/DOMAIN/evidence/WO-...-evaluator-upgrade.json [--json]\n492\t```\n493\t\n494\tThe first form is a read-only plan. `--apply` is an explicit transactional repository mutation. Same-identity managed repair needs no new lifecycle packet. When the installed target evaluator differs from the standard lock, apply additionally requires a distinct approved or in-progress work order with an exact `[evaluator_upgrade]` packet and a work-order-keyed JSON evidence path. The packet binds the prior lock SHA-256 and exact immutable target archive/payload identity with `scope = \"standard-root-only\"`; a product release decision cannot substitute for it.\n495\t\n496\tApply requires the already-published target evaluator installed from exact wheel bytes outside the checkout, changes only eligible managed content, and stops without a partial managed update when identity, authority, customization, or conflict prevents a safe plan. Transition evidence, managed files, and the lock share the recoverable transaction, and successful replay must be a no-op. Every repository, including the `se_harness` implementation repository, follows this transaction and uses one exact released evaluator. GitHub discovers the managed workflow beside existing repository-owned workflows, while required-check and workflow-ordering policy remains external. See [installation and safe upgrades](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md).\n497\t\n498\t## Retained skill ownership\n499\t\n500\t```text\n501\tharnessctl skill-ownership TARGET --provider plugin --plugin-root DIRECTORY [--apply] [--json]\n502\tharnessctl skill-ownership TARGET --provider repository [--apply] [--json]\n503\t```\n504\t\n505\tThis candidate command is unavailable in released 0.17.0. It removes the two\n506\tnamed harness skill directories under .agents/skills and .claude/skills,\n507\tincluding edits and extra files. Other skill directories remain unchanged.\n508\tThe replacement must contain a Verity Plane manifest and the six required files.\n509\tPreview is optional. Apply reads current inputs, deletes the old copies, and\n510\tsaves the portable provider choice last. Rerun the command after an interruption.\n511\tRestoration copies the current repository templates over disposable old copies.\n512\tThis file-only operation grants no lifecycle authority and does not install a\n513\tplugin or change host settings. See [the current design](plugin-simplification-2026-09-13.md).\n514\t\n515\t## Predecessor-to-successor migration rehearsal\n516\t\n517\tThe former `rehearse-recovery` command is retired (`WO-ECP-030`, issue #376; it had no workflow caller and no retained report), as the former `rehearse-migration` command was (`WO-ECP-010`, issue #210); the root-evaluator handover is rehearsed by `python -m repository_tools.upgrade_rehearsal`, a repository-owned tool described in [rehearsing the root-evaluator handover](evaluator-migration-rehearsal.md), not by a `harnessctl` subcommand.\n518\t\n519\t\n520\t## Domain and artifact authoring\n521\t\n522\t```text\n523\tharnessctl scaffold-domain [TARGET] --domain DOMAIN [--title TITLE] [--dry-run] [--json]\n524\tharnessctl create-artifact [TARGET] --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE [--id ID] [--dry-run] [--quiet] [--json]\n525\t```\n526\t\n527\tDomain slugs, artifact identifiers, type prefixes, templates, and destinations are validated before mutation. `create-artifact` creates only an incomplete `draft`; it does not choose owners, relations, content, approval, or authority. After creation it prints the created type's checklist from `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`, resolved in the selected wheel for the external layout or in the repository for a supported older layout; `--quiet` suppresses it. Existing valid flat layouts remain discoverable and are not automatically migrated.\n528\t\n529\tWithout `--id`, `create-artifact` allocates the lowest free\n530\t`TYPE-DOMAIN-NNN` across every local branch and tag and the working tree,\n531\tuntracked files included (`WO-ECP-002`): the refs are enumerated with\n532\t`git for-each-ref` and each ref's `docs/engineering` tree is listed, so two\n533\tagents on two branches cannot take the same number; remote-tracking refs are\n534\tnot consulted. The domain token is read from the domain's existing\n535\tartifacts. The result names the refs on which the next-lower identifier was\n536\tfound, so a gap is explained. Outside a Git checkout allocation is refused\n537\t(`WEX-ECP-013`) rather than guessed from the working tree. An explicit `--id`\n538\tis refused when any local ref already carries it.\n539\t\n540\tNon-dry-run authoring uses the common pre-write mutation guard. The invoking environment must match the schema-3 released-evaluator identity locked by the target repository; candidate source and editable or contaminated installs fail without creating the requested path.\n541\t\n542\t## Release unit derivation\n543\t\n544\t```text\n545\tharnessctl release-unit [TARGET] --from TAG --to COMMIT [--exempt SHA ...] [--contract REL-ID] [--json | --toml]\n546\t```\n547\t\n548\tMeasures the work-order trailers between the previous release tag and a\n549\tcandidate commit, including merged work. The JSON shape remains compatible.\n550\tUntraced commits, incomplete census information, and contract differences are\n551\tadvisory and exit successfully; invalid Git refs or command inputs still fail.\n552\t`--exempt` remains readable for old invocations but is unnecessary. The owner\n553\tapproves final release scope, and the final candidate still needs verification.\n554\t\n555\t## Runtime identity\n556\t\n557\t```text\n558\tharnessctl identity --role released-evaluator|candidate-source|candidate-package \\\n559\t  --expected-version VERSION --expected-root PATH [options] [--json]\n560\t```\n561\t\n562\tKey role-specific options are `--checkout-root`, `--candidate-commit`, `--evaluator-wheel-sha256`, `--entry-point`, `--require-isolated-python`, and `--require-entry-point`. The command verifies declared runtime origin; it does not select an evaluator or approve a candidate.\n563\t\n564\tRuntime identity also observes the running interpreter's own entry-point path through the declared interpreter-safety rule and records three additional facts: whether the entry point is a symbolic link, which position class its resolved target occupies relative to the expected and checkout roots, and the target's SHA-256. The schema identifier stays `se-harness-runtime-identity-v3`, because consumers require a subset of the identity rather than an exact field set. The observation is recorded for every role, but only the two environment-bounded roles — `released-evaluator` and `candidate-package` — turn a refusal into the `RID024` diagnostic; `candidate-source` has no environment boundary, because its expected root is the checkout itself. `RID004` and `RID006` keep their existing meanings unchanged.\n565\t\n566\t## Role-specific release qualification\n567\t\n568\t```text\n569\tharnessctl qualify released-root [ROOT] [--output PATH] [--json]\n570\tharnessctl qualify complete-candidate [ROOT] --candidate-commit FULL_COMMIT [--output PATH] [--json]\n571\tharnessctl qualify candidate-package --candidate-wheel PATH --candidate-commit FULL_COMMIT --candidate-wheel-sha256 SHA256 --verifier-wheel-sha256 SHA256 [--checkout-root PATH] [--output PATH] [--json]\n572\tharnessctl qualify public-install [ROOT] --release-record RLS-... --public-wheel PATH --public-wheel-sha256 SHA256 --payload-sha256 SHA256 [--output PATH] [--json]\n573\t```\n574\t\n575\tThe four subcommands are separate closed parsers. They bind evaluator identity, target identity, fixed checks, and one independence class before reporting a result. They do not accept a general evaluator, validator, script, omission, or diagnostic-allowlist option. `--output` must name a new external file; the command never overwrites it or writes qualification evidence inside the inspected repository.\n576\t\n577\t`--evaluator-python` is judged by the declared interpreter-safety rule before anything is spawned. Supply the environment's own lexical entry point — `bin/python` on POSIX, `Scripts/python.exe` on Windows — not the resolved system interpreter it points at. The environment root is derived from that lexical path, so an interpreter reached through a linked or junctioned parent directory is refused, as is one inside the inspected checkout or whose resolved target lands inside it. The terminal interpreter link itself is permitted, which is what makes an ordinary `python -m venv` environment usable on POSIX.\n578\t\n579\tAll operations emit `se-harness-release-qualification-v1`. The result identifies the operation, completion, outcome, evaluator, target, ordered checks, independence boundary, and its evidence-only authority. `complete-candidate` is always `candidate-controlled`, even when it passes. See [release qualification roles](release-qualification-roles.md) for the workflow map. `WO-REB-028` retired a fifth operation, `predecessor-view`, with the predecessor-bootstrap release path; its `PV001` and `PV002` codes stay reserved and no code path emits them.\n580\t\n581\tThe pre-namespace `accept-candidate` entry point, kept as a one-cycle alias of `qualify\n582\tcandidate-package` under `REQ-REB-022`, was removed after 0.11.0 (`WO-ECP-019`); its tombstone guard left with\n583\t0.15.0 (`WO-ECP-025`), so the parser now refuses the name as unknown. Exact public 0.6.0 predates the `qualify` namespace;\n584\tits immutable command still emits `se-harness-functional-acceptance-v1` and is accepted only as\n585\texplicitly labeled bootstrap evidence in the candidate workflow's legacy branch, which runs only a\n586\tverifier without `qualify`. That historical output is not converted into or described as canonical\n587\tqualification evidence.\n588\t\n589\t## Commit-bound verification preparation\n590\t\n591\t```text\n592\tharnessctl capture-verification [TARGET] \\\n593\t  --id VREC-... \\\n594\t  --work-order WO-... \\\n595\t  --verification VER-... \\\n596\t  --evidence PATH \\\n597\t  [--owner ROLE] [--domain DOMAIN] [--output PATH] [--json]\n598\t```\n599\t\n600\tRefusals distinguish invalid state (`WEX301`), Git provenance (`WEX302`),\n601\tevidence (`WEX303`), and record inputs (`WEX304`). Repeat work orders, contracts,\n602\tand evidence paths for a final aggregate candidate. Work may be implemented,\n603\tverified, or released; all declared verification contracts must be selected.\n604\tEvidence may be a shared integration report plus earlier verification records.\n605\tThe command writes a ready VREC and evaluator evidence. It does not verify it.\n606\t\n607\tAfter WO-KIS-009, each selected WO's recorded execution approval and unchanged\n608\tscope authorize preparation for either a person or an agent. There is no\n609\tactor-specific single-WO limit. Use the installed evaluator's procedure on a\n610\trepository still governed by an earlier release until normal upgrade.\n611\tUse `--candidate-commit COMMIT --test-command <argv...>` to test the exact final\n612\tintegration in a temporary checkout, including when the caller has local edits.\n613\t\n614\tFor a harmless rebase, use\n615\t`harnessctl refresh-verification REPO --from VREC-OLD-001 --id VREC-NEW-001`.\n616\tThis compares relevant Git tree entries, governing inputs, and retained evidence.\n617\tIt preserves the old ready record and writes a new ready successor. Changed\n618\trelevant files require fresh tests; verified records cannot be refreshed.\n619\t\n620\tAn accountable assurance owner reviews the retained evidence and separately decides whether to transition the VREC to `verified`. The record lives in later governance history and continues to bind the earlier candidate commit C.\n621\t\n622\tIf a later verified or released VREC fully covers a prepared ready record, the assurance owner may instead apply the declared `ready -> superseded` transition and name that successor with `--reason`. The command preserves `prepared_at` and `prepared_by`, adds only the supersession decision fields, typed successor relation, lifecycle event, status, and update date, and does not add `verified_at` or `verified_by`. Supersession means the proposal was retired, not verified. Historical superseded VRECs without preparation fields may retain the older valid `verified_at` capture shape; validation does not rewrite them or fabricate `verified_by`.\n623\t\n624\t## Commit-bound release preparation\n625\t\n626\t```text\n627\tharnessctl prepare-release [TARGET] \\\n628\t  --id RLS-... \\\n629\t  --release-contract REL-... \\\n630\t  --verification-record VREC-... \\\n631\t  --work-order WO-... \\\n632\t  --version VERSION \\\n633\t  --owner ROLE \\\n634\t  [--tag TAG] [--domain DOMAIN] [--output PATH] [--json]\n635\t```\n636\t\n637\tThe corresponding release refusal codes are `WEX401` to `WEX404`. Select one\n638\tverified or released final-candidate VREC and repeat `--work-order` for the\n639\trelease scope. The final record must cover exactly that work and all its\n640\tverification contracts. The RLS binds its exact candidate commit. Earlier\n641\trecords may be cited as supporting evidence at different commits; passing\n642\ttheir individual checks cannot replace final integration verification.\n643\t\n644\tBefore writing, the command proves the locked released evaluator including its wheel filename and SHA-256. It writes canonical normalized evaluator evidence and binds the evidence path and digest in the `status = \"ready\"` RLS. The record contains `prepared_at` and `prepared_by`; it omits `released_at` and `authorized_by` until a separate release transition. For the external layout, explicitly select `--integration git` or establish an equivalent owner rule before evidence writes. The selected `.gitattributes` fragment applies exactly `docs/engineering/**/evidence/*.json text eol=lf`, preserving canonical evidence bytes across supported checkouts so the raw SHA-256 survives. Independent validation and publication replay reject missing, changed, noncanonical, candidate-role, host-path-leaking, or lock-mismatched evidence. A rejected contract can support only its exact rejected RLS as terminal history and remains invalid for preparation, binding, release, publication, or credential-bearing use. The command does not transition the record to `released`, commit, push, tag, create a GitHub Release, publish to PyPI, or deploy.\n645\t\n646\tOnly `ready` and `released` release records claim a version. Valid rejected records remain immutable audit history and do not prevent one correctly bound active successor for an unpublished version; a second active record still fails.\n647\t\n648\t`WO-REB-028` retired the repository-specific schema-2 bootstrap path that once worked around released 0.5.0's inability to parse a rejected record: the predecessor preparation, assessment and publication-view adapters, their entry-point scripts, and the `qualify predecessor-view` operation are gone. Generic `harnessctl prepare-release` was never altered by that path and is unchanged by its removal. The retained 0.6.0 records keep their bytes and their hash-bound evidence digests; they are verifiable and no longer re-derivable. The real upgrade rehearsal, `python -m repository_tools.upgrade_rehearsal` (see [rehearsing the root-evaluator handover](evaluator-migration-rehearsal.md)), is the one mechanism for predecessor-to-successor assurance.\n649\t\n650\t## Authority summary\n651\t\n652\t| Result | Meaning |\n653\t| --- | --- |\n654\t| successful check | derived observation about the inspected repository or runtime |\n655\t| generated dashboard | derived navigation and anomaly evidence |\n656\t| generated `draft` | incomplete authoring starting point |\n657\t| generated `ready` VREC/RLS | structurally prepared proposal awaiting accountable review |\n658\t| human transition to `verified` | assurance decision about the exact candidate and evidence |\n659\t| human transition to `released` | release authorization for that same candidate |\n660\t\n661\tFor lifecycle timing, see [operational phasing](harness-operational-phasing.md). For complete examples, see [practical SE Harness examples](harness-lineage-example.md).\n662\t\n663\t\n664\tTo capture while keeping local edits, add `--candidate-commit COMMIT` and put\n665\t`--test-command EXECUTABLE ARGUMENTS...` last. Capture tests that commit in a\n666\ttemporary checkout and retains the command result in the record. A failed test\n667\twrites no record; uncommitted caller content is not used as tested evidence.\n668\t\n669\t## Explicit resource migration (successor candidate)\n670\t\n671\t```text\n672\tharnessctl upgrade TARGET --external-resources --prior-wheel PRIOR_WHEEL [--retire-file PATH] [--integration git|ci|pr] [--json]\n673\t```\n674\t\n675\tPreview first. Add `--apply` and `--instruction-delivery-evidence RECEIPT` to the\n676\tsame reviewed selection to retire its local entry. `--prior-wheel` must match\n677\tthe old selection; it is read as data to recognize stock bytes. Repeat\n678\t`--retire-file` only for explicitly selected unchanged editable seeds. Customized\n679\tinstruction seeds refuse migration. Historical and owner files stay intact.\n680\tSee the [migration procedure and resource map](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#migrate-a-repository-copy-installation).\n681\tOn an external-resource installation, `upgrade --integration git` previews the\n682\tGit attributes needed before hash-bound evidence. Repeat with `--apply` to write.\n683\t\n684\t## Editable files and lightweight identity (repository-copy layouts)\n685\t\n686\t`harnessctl upgrade TARGET --replace-file PATH` previews replacement of one\n687\teditable supplied file. Add `--apply` to write it; repeat the option for more\n688\tfiles. Other guidance, templates, CI and owner settings are kept. The selected\n689\tchecker version still has to match the installation record.\n690\t\n691\tOrdinary writes use checker origin/version. `doctor`, explicit `identity`,\n692\tinstallation, upgrade and release preparation check the full installed payload.\n693\tThe module route works without a console launcher. Runtime identity schema v4\n694\treports Python version without hashing the executable. New evaluator evidence\n695\tschema v2 binds canonical validated values; legacy schema v1 remains readable.\n696\t\n697\t## Hosted lifecycle rehearsal (candidate client)\n698\t\n699\tThese commands belong to the separately installed candidate client. The selected\n700\treleased evaluator remains 0.22.1 and is the service's sole lifecycle evaluator.\n701\t\n702\t```text\n703\tCLIENT_PYTHON -I -m se_harness remote rehearse --endpoint ENDPOINT --project PROJECT_ID --token-env TOKEN_VARIABLE --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --test-copy --request REQUEST_JSON --json\n704\tCLIENT_PYTHON -I -m se_harness remote operation --endpoint ENDPOINT --project PROJECT_ID --token-env TOKEN_VARIABLE --key ORIGINAL_KEY --json\n705\tCLIENT_PYTHON -I -m se_harness remote export --endpoint ENDPOINT --project PROJECT_ID --token-env TOKEN_VARIABLE --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --test-copy --request EXPORT_JSON --destination NEW_DIRECTORY --json\n706\t```\n707\t\n708\tUse the [closed v2 contract](../../server/contracts/lifecycle-v2.md) for request\n709\tfields, modes and allowed effects. `inspect` reports evaluator results. `preview`\n710\tstages a disposable result without changing graph state. `apply` requires the\n711\treturned preview digest and unchanged inputs. Only `apply` creates an accepted\n712\toperation receipt. A retry with identical inputs returns that receipt; different\n713\tinputs under its key fail. No arbitrary command or `--test-command` is forwarded.\n714\t\n715\tExport requires an immutable baseline and a new directory. It writes exact files,\n716\ta Git bundle and a manifest. Download success does not claim successful independent\n717\treplay. All these records are test data; Git remains authoritative for real work.\n718\t\n719\t## Concise hosted authoring\n720\t\n721\tThe candidate client supports explicit typed inputs for existing operations.\n722\tThis does not change service schemas, select lifecycle actions or grant authority.\n723\tUse the installed candidate Python with `-I -m se_harness remote OPERATION`.\n724\tCommon selection is `--endpoint URL --project UUID --token-env VARIABLE`.\n725\tCredentials stay in that environment variable. The service remains a private\n726\tloopback sandbox; Git remains authoritative.\n727\t\n728\t| Operation | Required typed fields |\n729\t| --- | --- |\n730\t| `remote import` | `--source-manifest FILE` |\n731\t| `remote draft-open` | `--baseline ID --work-order WO-ID` |\n732\t| `remote create-artifact` | `--context UUID --context-version N --domain NAME --artifact-type TYPE`; optional `--artifact ID` |\n733\t| `remote revise-artifact` | `--context UUID --context-version N --artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION --document-file FILE` |\n734\t| `remote read` (revision) | `--artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION` and exactly one of `--baseline ID` or `--context UUID --context-version N` |\n735\t\n736\tSelect `--typed`. Every mutation also requires `--operation-key KEY`,\n737\t`--expected-project-version N`, `--evaluator-file FILE`, and `--client-wheel FILE`.\n738\tThe evaluator file contains exactly `version`, `archive_sha256`, `payload_sha256`\n739\tfrom the selected combination. The client verifies the executing package against\n740\tits wheel. The source manifest uses the existing canonical manifest schema.\n741\tDocument files are exact UTF-8 bytes, at most 1 MiB. Linked paths are refused.\n742\tThe client constructs the existing wire request; the agent selects its meaning,\n743\tversions and key. It never retries or changes these inputs automatically.\n744\t\n745\tRaw `--request FILE` remains available for every existing operation, including\n746\tfreeze and test-copy lifecycle operations. Do not combine raw and typed input.\n747\tInvalid typed fields fail before a network request. Stale versions and reused\n748\tkeys with changed content retain the service's normal refusal behavior.\n749\t\n750\tAdd `--compact --record-directory NEW_DIRECTORY` for an evidence-backed view.\n751\tThe parent directory must exist; the destination must not exist or traverse a\n752\tlink. It retains exact request/response bytes, decoded documents and capture\n753\tmetadata (exit, timings, uncertainty). The view shows small fields and documents,\n754\twith explicit pointers for omitted content. Required omitted findings still need\n755\treading. It is a presentation, not an independent verdict.\n756\tFor known workflow results with a selected instruction step, the view can leave\n757\tthe full instruction-step catalogue and evaluator-only inputs in `full_response`\n758\twhen their pointers are smaller. Their JSON pointers are listed in `omitted`.\n759\tThe response path is given once in `full_response`. The selected step, its\n760\tprerequisites, executable procedure, findings and next action stay in view.\n761\tFor draft-validation responses, `draft_review` identifies the evaluator's shape\n762\tand required-link checks and reports content review as `not_assessed`. An empty\n763\t`incomplete` list and `findings_complete: true` do not establish content readiness.\n764\tThe agent reviews the saved content against the applicable authoring checklist.\n765\t\n766\tFor `create-artifact`, optional `--include-document` performs one read of the\n767\texact created revision after an accepted creation. No other mutation occurs.\n768\tIts `document_read` field retains the independent response. A failed read does\n769\tnot undo creation. After a capture or transport failure, inspect retained results\n770\tand look up the original operation key; a remote effect may have committed.\n771\tDo not choose a new key to conceal an unknown outcome. An explicit separate\n772\trevision read remains available for verification.\n773\t\n774\t### Complete instruction sections\n775\t\n776\tFor a repository governed by a release that supports this option:\n777\t\n778\t```text\n779\tharnessctl resources REPO --section docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity --section docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#intent --json\n780\t```\n781\t\n782\tUse actual returned/selected headings. The example does not select a lifecycle\n783\tstep. `--section RESOURCE#heading` can repeat up to 12 times. Each complete section\n784\tincludes source path, selected release, digest and line range. Overlapping sections\n785\tare included once. The view also includes that file's **Read this when** and\n786\t**Before this action** sections when present and not already included. These\n787\tentry conditions retain their exact source bytes. The reader does not follow\n788\tlinks or choose a procedure; read applicable linked prerequisites separately.\n789\tUnknown or ambiguous headings and changed resources fail.\n790\tDo not mix `--section` with `--resource`/`--content`. Existing resource modes stay\n791\tavailable. This candidate option does not make an older released evaluator support it.\n792\tThe native test adapter can use the same installed reader on byte-verified staged\n793\treleased resources; that does not substitute candidate policy for the released evaluator.\n794\t"

A paired decision (DEC) in `open` for each risk created with\\n  `--with-decision`. None created where existing records cover the threats.\\n- **Transient working material:** The selection of reused risks (RISK),\\n  review notes, generated IDs and paths, and links awaiting new work order\\n  (WO) IDs. If no risks are identified, retain that result with the reviewed\\n  scope. Retain this material under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Identify what could go wrong within the selected change scope.\\n2. Check whether an existing risk (RISK) already records each threat and its\\n   follow-up. Reference that record instead of creating a duplicate.\\n3. For each new risk (RISK), describe the threat and why it matters.\\n4. Identify its follow-up owner.\\n5. Specify the owner's next action.\\n6. Identify the formal artifacts threatened by it.\\n7. Determine whether an unresolved decision must block those artifacts.\\n8. Preview the risk (RISK) with the command below. Inspect the proposed\\n   content, affected IDs, and destination paths.\\n9. Run the same command with the same arguments, removing only `--dry-run`.\\n10. Read every written file reported by the command. Retain its ID and path\\n    for the review handoff.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\nReplace the quoted text and `OWNER` with the risk description and identified\\nowner. Repeat `--threatens ARTIFACT-ID` for each threatened artifact. Omit that\\noption if no affected formal artifact exists yet:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl raise-risk REPO --domain DOMAIN --title \\\"Risk title\\\" --description \\\"What could go wrong and why it matters\\\" --action \\\"Next follow-up action\\\" --owner OWNER --threatens ARTIFACT-ID --dry-run --json\\n```\\n\\nAdd `--with-decision` only if action 7 identifies a decision (DEC) that must\\nblock the named artifacts. Use the same option in both preview and creation.\\nA risk (RISK) alone does not block work.\\n\\n**Completion:** Identified risks (RISK) have formal records with an owner and\\nnext action. If none were identified, retain `None identified` with the\\nreviewed scope as transient working material.\\n\\n**Later use:** Review any paired decision (DEC) in [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec). [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements) uses the\\nrisks (RISK) to define work and stop conditions and adds links that depend on\\nnew work order (WO) IDs.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8431175790f8bf07019c19f9cb51d6ee5186b8bc66fccfbb2665ab99fc5028e9\"}, {\"heading\": \"raised-risks\", \"title\": \"Raised risks\", \"anchor\": \"raised-risks\", \"start_line\": 176, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## Raised risks\\n\\nA risk (RISK) in `raised` may have no paired decision\\n(DEC). Recording that risk alone does not block work. Use\\n`raise-risk --with-decision` when creating a risk that needs a paired blocking\\ndecision.\\n\\nA raised risk MUST NOT have more than one paired decision in `open` or\\n`deferred`. When that decision exists, it names the risk in `concerns`, and\\nits `blocks` set MUST equal the risk's `threatens` set. Disposing the paired\\ndecision applies its recorded effect to the risk in the same operation.\\nThe blocked artifacts change state only through their own transitions.\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"dcbef84857f6b71fbfa2099de79f6caa4d82e8977b13465eccb762ffc3a9ea1e\"}, {\"heading\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"title\": \"Blocking decisions\", \"anchor\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"start_line\": 150, \"end_line\": 175, \"content\": \"## Blocking decisions\\n\\nA decision (DEC) in `open` blocks every transition\\nof the artifacts in its `blocks` relation. A decision (DEC) in `deferred`\\nblocks transitions outside its recorded permitted scope.\\n\\nFor example, a decision (DEC) names work order (WO) `WO-EXAMPLE-001` in both\\n`concerns` and `blocks`. It is deferred with the scope\\n`WO-EXAMPLE-001:approved-in_progress`. This deferral\\nallows the work order (WO) to move from `approved` to `in_progress` if all\\nother checks pass. It still blocks moving that work order (WO) from\\n`in_progress` to `implemented`. The deferral also records when the decision\\n(DEC) must be revisited. Deferral does not itself start the work.\\n\\nAn accepted deviation is a decision (DEC) with `kind = \\\"deviation\\\"`,\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"`, and `disposition.option = \\\"accept\\\"`.\\nIt records permission to depart from one identified specification (SPEC)\\nrule; \\u201caccepted\\u201d is not a separate lifecycle state for the decision (DEC).\\n\\nThat deviation remains applicable to the affected specification (SPEC),\\nwork orders (WO), and their verification records (VREC) and release records\\n(RLS) until a later decision (DEC) against the same rule reaches\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"` with `disposition.option` set to `amend` or\\n`supersede`. The disposition is written through `harnessctl decide`, not\\nby editing the metadata by hand.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ed29cb785085f0704b9ab61f95ab42f2ee01579c0d191cb6587ce6c97684cdc0\"}]}]}",

A legacy section, where one remains, reads `None` or lists `DEC-` identifiers; prose there is `E-DCM-004`.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"b3fdcc8578aac9039cf6513b13851f7a35a63027fde6dd1afeb34593a23e083b\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\claude-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"991b526d6280554dcca6901c1790e5519b8894e08635a1f10618aa84a29aaf28\", \"bytes\": 15212, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe proposed package needs validation, review or a human authorization decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8b18d925f39f314acc9ea6bcc9820015c4c9430d836144e85bc31b670752371b\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nFor reviewing each definition, use its selected [Type checklist](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#type-checklists). Before approving work, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). For an open or deferred decision, read [RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"9aa32693606102a5aa74b2e4a614aed6904471e5f618dea93356baac97c86ca2\"}, {\"heading\": \"resolve-approval-blockers\", \"title\": \"Resolve approval blockers\", \"anchor\": \"resolve-approval-blockers\", \"start_line\": 84, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Resolve approval blockers\\n\\n**Inputs:** The findings from [Assess the proposed artifact package](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#assess-the-proposed-artifact-package) and the affected draft artifacts or\\npending decisions (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Corrected drafts within the proposed scope. Where an\\n  actual human decision is supplied, the selected decision (DEC) receives its\\n  disposition. A paired risk (RISK) may change through that same operation.\\n- **Transient working material:** The resolution of each finding and any\\n  remaining dependency requiring an amendment or another human decision.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Correct incomplete or inconsistent draft content within the requested scope.\\n2. Return an accepted-definition change to the amendment procedure in\\n   \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Do not edit accepted authority to clear a check.\\n3. For a blocking decision (DEC), inspect its current question and options.\\n4. Obtain the accountable human's exact answer if it has not already been given.\\n5. Preview that disposition with the command below.\\n6. Apply the same command with `--apply` only if its inputs match the actual\\n   decision and the preview passes.\\n7. Read back the decision (DEC) and any paired risk (RISK).\\n8. Rerun the checks affected by the corrections. Preserve unresolved blockers.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a declared option ID. Add `--revisit \\\"Trigger\\\"` for acceptance of a\\ndeviation. A risk-mitigation option also requires `--mitigated-by WO-ID` for\\neach selected mitigating work order (WO). Review the returned operation before applying it.\\n\\nACTOR is the actual human who made the decision. If that human acts under an\\nexisting owner label, first resolve their authority under\\n[Decision rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights), then add\\n`--authority-owner OWNER` to both preview and apply. An unrelated label refuses without writing.\\n\\nFor an explicitly authorized deferral, use this preview instead:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO --revisit \\\"Trigger\\\" --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nRepeat `--scope` for each permitted transition. For an explicitly authorized\\nwithdrawal, replace the option or deferral arguments with `--withdraw`.\\nApply a passing preview by repeating the exact command with `--apply`.\\nThen inspect the decision (DEC) again and rerun validation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nIf proposing a departure from a `SHOULD` rule, record the rule ID, reason,\\nimpact, accountable human or agent, and compensating evidence. Present these\\nwith the affected review finding. Recording the departure does not authorize\\nan action or waive a required check.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each blocker is resolved or assigned an explicit outstanding\\ndecision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order`, `--verification`, and `--evidence` for every selected\\ninput. `EVIDENCE-PATH` is a repository-relative file, not a directory or an\\nindex whose links will be followed automatically. Capture writes immediately\\nafter its checks; it has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\nIf an unchanged rebase leaves an earlier ready record bound to the old\\ncandidate, use [Refresh verification after an unchanged rebase](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#refresh-verification-after-an-unchanged-rebase).\\nA verified source or changed relevant inputs cannot use that shortcut.\\n\\nIf preserving local edits requires the supported committed-candidate route,\\nuse `--candidate-commit COMMIT` with `--test-command EXECUTABLE ARGUMENTS`.\\nPut `--test-command` last. Confirm that the evidence applies to the selected candidate and environment.\\n4. Run missing checks using the verification contract's (VER) commands or\\n   manual procedure. Retain their actual results.\\n5. Record each criterion as passed, failed, or not assessed, with its reason.\\n6. Retain material findings and their resolution with the verification evidence.\\n7. For a defect requiring implementation changes, identify a work order that\\n   covers the correction and is eligible for execution. Follow the recovery\\n   rules under \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d A completed work order does not\\n   become executable again because verification found a defect.\\n8. After the authorized correction, establish the new candidate identity and\\n   reassess the affected criteria against evidence for that candidate.\\n\\n**Harness command:** None for the substantive assessment. Use the check\\ncommands and manual assessments defined in the verification contracts (VER).\\nHarness validation alone does not prove the required behavior.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every required criterion has evidence or a visible gap.\\nFailures and missing checks are not reported as passes.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the verification record](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#prepare-the-verification-record) binds the retained evidence to a verification record\\n(VREC). [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) uses it for the human's assessment.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"78a405625bfb24107f4b8f4f09ad84942d5710c55b27d58f3114da5f40688c3b\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"title\": \"Record the verification decision\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"start_line\": 255, \"end_line\": 300, \"content\": \"### Record the verification decision\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact human decision, ready verification record (VREC), and\\nunchanged candidate and evidence inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected verification record (VREC) receives\\n  its permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated record is retained through authorized Git\\n  actions. Inspect the verification record (VREC) and resulting workflow context.\\n5. Report its actual state, any blocker, and the evaluator's next action.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor supersession, select a successor verification record that is already\\n`verified` or `released` and preserves the old record\\u2019s work-order coverage.\\nUse the transition preview to assess that selection.\\n\\nFor `rejected`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to preview and apply.\\nFor `superseded`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=SUCCESSOR-VREC-ID\\\"` to both. Release-record preparation requires both.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Release path:** One release record (RLS) in `ready` and its generated\\n  evaluator evidence, when preparation is required and succeeds.\\n- **Retained files:** Required build or delivery evidence at the authorized\\n  locations. Builds occur only when separately covered by the selected scope.\\n- **Transient working material:** Preparation notes, proposed external content,\\n  and inspected write destinations.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm authority for the exact preparation operation. Obtain a missing\\n   human decision before writing; reuse matching authority already supplied.\\n2. Inspect existing records and outputs before creating replacements.\\n3. For release, select an active release contract (REL), version, domain,\\n   and unused release record (RLS) ID. Check local Git refs and existing\\n   version reservations before choosing the ID and version.\\n4. Select the final eligible verification record (VREC) for the candidate.\\n   Its work-order (WO) set must exactly cover the work being released.\\n5. Confirm all intended output paths and the clean working-tree condition\\n   required by release preparation.\\n6. Run the release preparation command. Inspect its written record, evidence,\\n   candidate identity, and `ready` state.\\n7. Retain the new release record (RLS) and evidence in an authorized governance\\n   commit after the candidate they describe.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor release preparation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl prepare-release REPO --id RLS-ID --release-contract REL-ID --verification-record VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --version VERSION --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order` for every released work order (WO). This evaluator requires one final verification record (VREC) covering the complete\\nrelease. Earlier records remain supporting evidence. If that coverage is\\nmissing, return to verification instead of inventing or relabelling it.\\n\\nAdd `--tag TAG` only for an explicitly selected tag value; this records the\\nvalue and does not create a Git tag. `prepare-release` writes after its checks;\\nit has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\n**Completion:** The required delivery inputs are prepared, or a precise\\npreparation blocker is known. Preparation performs no merge, publication,\\ndeployment, or release decision.\\n\\n**Later use:** A ready release record (RLS) proceeds to [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required). \\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d3fcc6f4d9565acc0d714479b8b27df0173ce927ec4d36a757bf1f5710f34942\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"title\": \"Record the release decision, when required\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"start_line\": 117, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Record the release decision, when required\\n\\n**Inputs:** The human's exact decision and unchanged release inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected release record (RLS) receives the\\n  permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated release record (RLS), retained through\\n  authorized Git actions.\\n- **Transient working material:** The applied result and current next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the current release inputs with the human's reviewed inputs.\\n2. Preview the selected transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the release record (RLS) and report the actual resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor rejection, add `--reason \\\"RLS-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both transition\\ncommands. Related verification records (VREC) and work orders (WO) are not\\ntransitioned automatically.\\n\\nFor a complete-release decision, use the existing `--reason` input to retain the\\nactual human decision reference and reviewed delivery-plan path and SHA-256.\\nThis is retained evidence of the supplied decision, not permission derived by\\nparsing arbitrary reason text. Preserve the referenced plan bytes for each later\\nauthority comparison. No new approval file or lifecycle state is needed.\\n\\n**Completion:** The release decision is recorded or explicitly refused.\\nNo Git tag, publication, or deployment has been performed by this transition.\\n\\n**Later use:** A released record may support [Confirm authority for the external action](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-authority-for-the-external-action)'s external-action checks.\\nRejection follows the evaluator's remediation procedure.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"41884593e91b2762c5d0406d1b6e73f0f7731edf06676a4cf15a64b0760c789d\"}]}]}",

  - My first export failed because its parent folder didn't exist and the helper can't create folders.
- There were no host permission denials.
- The service's `check` can't assess a planned file list before approval. I relied on the actual change set at handoff, which was fully in scope.
- The release record format requires a tag value, so I recorded `v0.0.1`. That only stores the text; no Git tag was created.
- The seven read-only tool replies came back inline, not as files. `work/mcp-reads.json` holds the exact requests and the key fields copied from the replies, not byte-exact copies.

Files are in `work/`:
- native-report.md
- native-observations.json
- mcp-reads.json
- 66-observations — the call log; it doesn't include the report writes made after it
